newsitem.title: USA: Regulators set hearing for ComEd plant.
newsitem.headline: Regulators set hearing for ComEd plant.

text.p: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission said Monday it will meet March 19 with representatives of Commonwealth Edison Co to discuss apparent violations at ComEd's nuclear power station in Zion, Ill.

The meeting will focus on apparent violations of NRC shipping and radiation protection requirements which were identified during an NRC inspection in December and January, the NRC said in a statement.
No decisions on the apparent violations will be made at this conference. Those decisions will be made by senior NRC officials at a later date, it said.

The apparent violations, among others, include using an outdated shipping procedure for radioactive materials; shipping radioactive material that exceeded radiation limits for that type of shipment, and failing to measure representative samples of water treatment resins, it said.

The meeting is defined as a predecisional enforcement conference and does not mean the NRC has determined that a violation has occurred or that enforcement action will be taken, the NRC said. Rather, the purpose is to discuss apparent violations and to enable the company to outline its proposed corrective actions, the NRC said.
Commonwealth Edison, a subsidiary of Unicom Corp, was not immediately available to comment.
